papers.title: Mandatory Carbon Disclosure and the Cost of Capital
papers.path: sources/Ingram and Okonkwo 2024 JSA, Mandatory carbon disclosure.pdf
papers.abstract: We exploit a staggered national rollout of mandatory carbon disclosure to estimate its effect on the cost of equity capital. Firms brought into scope report a decline in implied cost of capital of roughly 38 basis points relative to not-yet-treated peers, concentrated among firms with previously sparse voluntary reporting. The effect is larger where an assurance requirement accompanies the mandate, and absent where disclosure is unaudited. We interpret this as evidence that the credibility of the disclosure, not its existence, is what investors price.

papers.title: What Firms Say When They Say Nothing: Boilerplate in Climate Risk Reporting
papers.path: sources/Vasquez, Lindqvist and Osei 2023 A&S, What firms say.pdf
papers.abstract: We measure textual similarity across climate risk disclosures in 6,400 annual reports and document that a large share of reported climate risk is boilerplate: near-identical language recycled across firms and years. Boilerplate intensity rises sharply in the first year a firm is required to disclose and falls only where an activist investor or a regulator has previously challenged the filing. Firms with high boilerplate intensity show no relationship between their stated risks and their subsequent physical loss events.

papers.title: Measuring Assurance Quality in Sustainability Reports: A Framework
papers.path: sources/Haugen and Petrov 2025 REA, Measuring assurance quality.pdf
papers.abstract: Assurance over sustainability reporting is widely required and poorly measured. We propose a framework that separates assurance scope, assurance depth, and assurer competence, and show that the three components move independently across a sample of 2,100 assured reports. Studies that collapse them into a single binary indicator will understate the variation that matters. We provide a coding scheme and report inter-coder reliability.
